subject: Follow-up: Cost acceptance thresholds + host comparison
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ella Johnson <ella.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Cost acceptance thresholds + host comparison

Hi Ella —

Thanks again for taking time earlier today. Quick recap from our end and two asks so we can scope a concrete pilot: 

Recap (from the demo)
- Primary workload: patient chart summarization + eligibility checks via multi-turn chat.
- Typical request size: 1.5k tokens / session on average; peaks up to ~8k for long transcripts.
- Target latency: sub-400ms for 95th on concise prompts (we discussed relaxed SLAs for long transcripts).

Cost discussion takeaways
- You mentioned internal cost sensitivity and wanting a target that keeps your per-feature cost predictable.
- For benchmarking: OpenAI and Anthropic model lists are serving as your references; you flagged $/1M token targets as the primary decision point.

Two asks to move forward
1) Can you confirm an expected monthly token volume range (low / mid / high) for the pilot? Example buckets that help us: 50M / 250M / 1B tokens per month.
2) What is your internal target $ per 1M tokens (ballpark is fine) that would make Redwood a straightforward fit versus continuing with hosted partners?

To make this concrete for you, we’ll produce a short cost-acceptance matrix comparing:
- Redwood hosted (standard models + recommended quantized variant)
- Redwood dedicated (reserved pool with committed throughput)
- Representative host comparison (OpenAI, Anthropic, and a self-hosting proxy cost for an open-model host)

If you can reply with the two items above, I’ll turn around a short matrix + recommended pilot configuration and a sample commitment model (monthly seat/commit + $/1M tiers).

Attachments: I’m attaching a working cost projection (acme_cost_projection_v2.xlsx) and our one-page pricing deck (redwood-pricing-deck-1p.pdf) that show how we fold batching, KV cache, and prefix caching into unit economics.

Proposed next steps:
- You reply with volume & target $/1M tokens (today’s ask)
- We send a 1-week pilot proposal w/ SLA/targets and pilot success metrics

Thanks,
Ben
---
Ben Carter
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Ella Johnson <ella.johnson@acmehealth.com>

Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Cost acceptance thresholds + host comparison

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Quick answers below: 

1) Probable monthly token volume (pilot):
- Low: 40–60M tokens (sandbox + internal QA)
- Mid: 200–300M tokens (limited production for a subset of clinics)
- High: 900M–1.2B tokens (full roll-out projection for 12 months out)

2) Target $/1M tokens:
- Leadership has given a budget band we have to respect. Our internal procurement target for a long-term partner is $/1M tokens in the low double-digits — roughly $10–$18 per 1M depending on model capability.

For context, we currently see list-like numbers where OpenAI (for their higher-capability models) is landing at the higher end of that band when you include prompt+response tokens, and some Anthropic references are mid-band. We are also poking at open-model hosting partners that, when you strip infra and engineering overhead, claim to get into single-digit $/1M — but those come with integration and reliability tradeoffs we want to avoid for a regulated health workload.

Procurement will likely want a 3-month pilot with a committed minimum. They asked me to also capture: preferred payment cadence (monthly), basic SOC2 evidence, and a pilot SLA.

Happy to have Sergio and Laura looped in — they were on the demo and will help on procurement/technical follow-up.

— Ella

Sergio / Laura — forwarding Ella's reply (below) with their volume bands and target range. Procurement will want SOC2 + monthly billing cadence + 3-month pilot minimum.

Key negotiation targets I think make sense:
- Aim to offer the mid-band for pilot: $12/1M tokens as an introductory committed price at ~200–300M tokens/mo.
- If they commit to >750M tokens/month on Dedicated, propose stepped pricing down to $6–7/1M (via reserved capacity + quantization profile).
- Include an explicit fallback to Redwood hosted (no infra ops) as part of pilot to address their reliability/regulatory risk.

Laura — can you prepare two short quote options (one hosted pilot @ 200–300M tokens/mo @ $12/1M and one dedicated reserved @ 750M/mo with stepped pricing outline)? Please include an estimated monthly infra/Ops runbook note (how we handle KV cache, prefix caching, and expected token latency envelope) — that helps procurement.

Sergio — can you draft a 3-bullet margin/discount rationale we can present to leadership (why we can step down to $6–7 at scale)? I want a couple of bullets tied to batching, caching efficiency, and model quantization strategy.

I’ll assemble the matrix and send back to Ella first thing tomorrow morning.

— Ben

Subject: Pilot proposal & cost-acceptance matrix — Acme Health (next steps)

Hi Ella / Procurement team —

Thanks for the quick answers. Attached are two short artifacts: a one-page cost-acceptance matrix (redwood-pricing-deck-1p.pdf) and a working cost projection workbook (acme_cost_projection_v2.xlsx). High level proposal summary below.

Pilot option A — Hosted pilot (recommended quick start)
- Target pilot volume: 200–300M tokens / month
- Intro price: $12 / 1M tokens for the pilot term (3 months)
- Success metrics: 95th latency < 500ms for <2k token sessions; qualitative accuracy checks on 200 eval prompts; operational handoff checklist for compliance
- Pros: fastest time-to-value, no infra ops for Acme
- Cons: less control over dedicated throughput at scale

Pilot option B — Reserved dedicated (for scale & unit economics)
- Favorable economics at commit: stepped pricing, e.g., $10 / 1M at 500M/mo, $7 / 1M at 750M/mo, and $6 / 1M at 1B+/mo (requires 12-month commit for the lowest tier)
- Includes priority capacity reservation and access to model-quantization recommendations and an ops runbook

Competitive note (quick benchmarking)
- OpenAI (higher-capability hosted models): typically higher list per-1M in this capability band; effective $/1M for Acme-like workloads often ends up in the upper-teens once you account for prompt/response tokens on chat-style flows.
- Anthropic: mid-band benchmarking; capability/pricing varies by model family.
- Self-hosted open-model hosts: can show single-digit $/1M claims but require engineering and sustained infra costs — often hidden as >$ spent on infra + ops.

Next steps / asks from Acme
- Confirm which pilot option you prefer (A or B) and the pilot start window (target week).
- Confirm any minimum contractual language needed for SOC2 evidence or PO timelines (procurement indicated monthly billing cadence).
- If you prefer, we can put a short 3-month MSA + SOW in place and swap to a reserved capacity contract on an agreed date.

I’ll set up a 30-minute pilot kickoff call next week if that helps — suggested times: Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward to moving this to a short pilot.

Best,
Ben
